rationale: This is a one-variable swap (ceq→ib) on the archived "Cash-Composition Book Value" and, unlike book equity, `ib` is frequently negative, so multiplying by the positive cash-share term inverts the intended ordering for loss-making firms and makes the composite non-monotone in the value dimension.

The sign conventions are handled correctly (NEG(invch) = inventory build, NEG(apalch) = payable runoff) and the conjunctive MIN is a genuine structural change rather than a relabeling of the additive "Unfunded Inventory Build Yield," though it targets a very sparse tail and coverage/portfolio stability are likely to deteriorate further from the parent's already-thin 0.06.

This is a near-cosmetic edit of the archived "Short-Debt-Funded Accrual Trap" — replacing DELTA(dlc) with DELTA(dlc)−DELTA(dltt) inside the same MIN construction — offered without any diagnosis of why the parent's fmb (−1.24) and alpha t (−1.93) fell short.

The premise is factually wrong — Compustat `dp` is already "Depreciation and Amortization," so `dpc − dp` is a near-zero reclassification residual with a large point mass at zero, yielding a signal that is mostly definitional noise rather than an intangible-consumption burden.

The multiplier NEG(NWC/at) changes sign across firms, so within the majority (positive-NWC) population a *higher* sales yield pushes the composite *lower*, directly contradicting the stated value hypothesis; the underlying idea is also close to the published operating-liability-leverage effect.

Replacing the one-period accrual charge with a non-negative distance-from-three-period-minimum is a substantive persistence-based reformulation of the archived accrual-financing-adjusted yield, but the adjustment is small relative to market cap for most firms, so the signal risks being a near-collinear restatement of plain earnings yield and should be tested against E/P as a control.
